subject: Renewal: phased audit-log curation, hot/cold retention split, and renewal path
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@nimblefin.com>, procurement@nimblefin.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-05T09:02:00Z
Subject: Renewal kickoff: audit-log curation and retention split proposal

Hi Emma / Nimble procurement team,

Thanks again for the heads-up about Nimble's upcoming renewal window. Per our conversation last week I wanted to lay out a proposed approach for the SOC 2 re-attestation evidence flow that minimizes operational overhead for your team while preserving audit fidelity. High level:

- Phased handoff: prioritize evidence related to access controls, change logs, and admin activity first (Phase A), followed by export of application-level audit logs (Phase B).
- Retention split: we propose a hot/cold model where 90 days of logs remain in hot storage for rapid pulls; older logs are archived to cold storage with read-on-demand retrieval. This reduces transfer volume for the attestation while meeting retention requirements.
- Burst capacity: for evidence transfer windows we can provision a temporary dedicated throughput lane (burst) for the export; we will bill it separately as a one-time uplift tied to the renewal.

Attachments: I included an evidence_checklist.xlsx and retention_tiers.csv that map the items by Phase A/B and suggested storage tier. Also added S3 transfer instructions.

Action items for Nimble: please confirm (1) whether Phase A items align with your auditor's prioritized list, (2) acceptance of the 90-day hot/archival split, and (3) whether procurement needs a formal amendment for one-time burst capacity billing.

If that sounds OK I can schedule a 30-minute sync with Rahul from Insight Assurance to confirm the auditor acceptance and lock dates.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Rahul Singh <rahul@insightassurance.com>

Date: 2027-09-06T11:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal kickoff: audit-log curation and retention split proposal

Hi Jordan / Emma,

Thanks for the clear plan. A few notes from the auditor side after a quick review of the checklist:

- Phase A looks good — admin activity, privileged access logs, and change management trails will be sufficient for the initial attestation scope.
- Regarding the 90-day hot window: acceptable from a sampling/audit perspective, provided the archived logs are cryptographically hashed and there is a documented retrieval SLA (<= 48 hours).
- For Phase B exports (application logs), we will need a sample of 14 consecutive days plus three high-load days. Please ensure timestamps are normalized (UTC) and that any internal service identifiers are mapped to Nimble's system names (mapping table helps).

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can Redwood produce the mapping table automatically from the log catalog, or will this be a manual handoff?
2) What does the one-time burst pricing look like (ballpark)? Nimble procurement will need that number to process the amendment.

Happy to join a call next week to finalize.

Best,
Rahul Singh
Lead Auditor, Insight Assurance
rahul@insightassurance.com

Rahul, Jordan, Emma —

Quick answers to the auditor questions:

1) Mapping table: Redwood can auto-generate a mapping output from our log-catalog export. It requires a short script run (we'll provide the script and the mapping CSV). The mapping will include service id -> Nimble system name, field schema, and timestamp normalization notes. I attached a sample mapping in the Drive link for reference.

2) Burst pricing: for the export window we typically price a dedicated throughput uplift as a fixed one-time line item. Ballpark for Nimble's expected 2TB export over 48 hours is $2,500 for the dedicated throughput lane + standard egress. If Nimble prefers, we can amortize a portion into a 12-month committed capacity add-on instead of a one-off charge.

Operational note: to hit the 48-hour retrieval SLA for archived logs we'll want to schedule the Phase B export no earlier than 72 hours after confirmation so we can run a pre-export integrity check.

Proposed timeline:
- Sep 9: audit scope call (30m) with Rahul and Emma
- Sep 12: Phase A handoff (access control + admin logs)
- Sep 20: Phase B export window (application logs), with the burst uplift provisioned Sep 19-21

Jordan — can you loop in procurement/legal if Nimble requests the amortized option? Emma — please confirm availability for Sep 9 or suggest an alternative.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Security Ops
Redwood Inference

Hi all — thanks for the clear plan and the numbers. Confirming:

- Sep 9, 10:00am PT works for the audit scope call (Rahul, joining remotely).
- We accept the 90-day hot / cold archival split as long as the retrieval SLA is in the contract appendix. Procurement will need the $2,500 burst line item as a one-time charge unless Redwood can provide the amortized pricing option in writing.
- Please send the mapping script and the sample mapping CSV ahead of the call so our engineering lead can validate field names.

Jordan / Vanessa — please put a short amendment draft in the HubSpot link (or attach to this thread) with the billing option spelled out and an appendix for the retrieval SLA. Once procurement reviews the line item we can push the renewal toward a signed amendment.

Thanks,
Emma Li
